column1: # The ATmega's event lines (docs/hubs/uart-protocol.md § Events) and what a key
# reader must make of each (#1020). Both readers run every row: the Python one
# in audio/tests/test_keys_reader.cpp. A parser change that moves one row fails
# both suites, so the two cannot drift apart unnoticed.
# One row: <line> TAB <outcome>. The line is sent with "\n" appended; in it
#   key R C down|up   a key event for (R, C); positions here are named ones
#   enc I D           an encoder event (the range check is the UI's, later)
#   malformed         a KP:/KR:/EN: line that did not parse: counted, dropped
#   ignored           not input (informational, or not ours): no event, no count
#   ready             the ATmega's boot banner (a reset)
# A field is an optional sign and 1-6 ASCII digits, nothing else; the line is
# stripped of ASCII whitespace at both ends first (Python's bytes.strip()).
